gifu-kakamigahara-air-space-museum.name: Gifu-Kakamigahara Air and Space Museum (Sora Haku)

rows.item: LE-7 rocket engine (listed as 実機 / actual hardware; the predecessor of LE-7A, not a 7A)
rows.notes: Museum page S1 lists 'LE-7 エンジン 実機' and 'H-II ロケット フェアリング 実機'. It is an LE-7, not an LE-7A; recorded under the LE-7A family only. The H-II fairing does not match an Orrery object (H-IIA).

rows.item: LE-7 engine recovered from the sea after H-II F8 (1999), in the Space Development Exhibition Room; large LE-5 and LE-7 engines outdoors
rows.notes: JAXA page confirms real engines (LE-5, LE-7) on display but does not say which units. The H-II F8 LE-7 is attested only by Commons (File:H-IIRocket_F8_LE-7engine.jpg, taken 2012, Kakuda exhibition room) and ja.wikipedia. LE-7, not LE-7A.

rows.item: Large LE-5 liquid rocket engine displayed outdoors (variant not stated)
rows.notes: JAXA says 'LE-5, LE-7' outdoors; the LE-5 variant (5/5A/5B) is not stated, so uncertain.

rows.item: H-IIB development/structural test vehicle (outdoor, since Nov 2011): real first-stage engine section, LH2 tank, central body, interstage and fairing; other parts replicas
rows.notes: Evidence is Wikipedia only (museum site returned 503 twice). It is the H-IIB variant, which shares the H-IIA technology base. Real vs replica split quoted from Wikipedia, not verified at the museum.

rows.item: LE-7A engines in the H-IIB structural test vehicle (per Wikipedia)
rows.notes: Wikipedia-only; not verified at the museum. The ja.wikipedia LE-7 page also has a 2006 caption of an LE-7 at this museum (outdated).
